events.title: Globe Theatre Destroyed by Fire
events.description: During a performance of Henry VIII, a cannon fired as a theatrical effect ignited the thatched roof of Shakespeare's Globe Theatre in London. The wooden building burned to the ground within about two hours, reportedly with no deaths.
events.significance: The loss of the playhouse associated with William Shakespeare's company is one of the most famous disasters in theatre history. The Globe was rebuilt in 1614, and a modern reconstruction opened in 1997.

events.title: Birth of Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
events.description: The French writer and aviator was born in Lyon, France. He became a pioneering airmail pilot and later wrote The Little Prince (1943), along with works such as Night Flight and Wind, Sand and Stars.
events.significance: The Little Prince became one of the best-selling and most translated books in history, and Saint-Exupéry's writing shaped literature about aviation, humanity, and friendship.

events.title: U.S. Supreme Court Decides Furman v. Georgia
events.description: The U.S. Supreme Court ruled 5-4 that the death penalty as then administered was arbitrary and capricious, constituting cruel and unusual punishment under the Eighth and Fourteenth Amendments.
events.significance: The decision effectively suspended capital punishment across the United States until states rewrote their statutes, leading to the 1976 Gregg v. Georgia ruling that allowed executions to resume.

events.title: First iPhone Goes on Sale
events.description: Apple released the original iPhone in the United States, with customers lining up outside stores. It combined a mobile phone, a widescreen iPod, and an internet communicator with a multi-touch screen interface.
events.significance: The iPhone transformed the mobile phone industry and helped launch the modern smartphone era, reshaping communication, media, software distribution, and daily life worldwide.

events.title: Space Shuttle Atlantis Docks with Mir
events.description: Space Shuttle Atlantis (STS-71) docked with the Russian space station Mir, the first shuttle-Mir docking. The mission exchanged crew members and marked the start of joint U.S.-Russian operations in orbit.
events.significance: The docking symbolized post-Cold War cooperation in space and provided experience that paved the way for the construction of the International Space Station.
